completed: THE `paint` STEP KIND (commit 67f0de71). MpiStepPaint mounts PaintManager + brushDab.js - the History paint tool's own RGBA layer and dab - on a plain canvas stage, the same relationship MpiStepCrop has with CropManager. No second brush. Binds through STEP_MEDIA, returns the layer ALONE as an RGBA PNG at the SOURCE's natural size. Controls are the gizmo's own one row (brush/eraser, colour, Undo, Clear); brush SIZE is the mouse wheel, matching InputController.

FlowStep.mediaRole added to the frame - the one change no handoff had foreseen. The merged graph takes TWO images (Input_Image AND Input_Paint) while _deriveRunMedia could only REPLACE a role's media, so a paint step bound to the photo would have eaten the photo. A step now names where its derived file lands and the frame APPENDS when that role is empty. Omit it and crop's behaviour is byte-identical.

VERIFIED LIVE in an isolated instance on :58669, not by inspection: layer back at the source's 1200x800, undo restoring a stroke to the pixel (19529 -> 32893 -> 19529), Clear and undo-after-Clear holding, the eraser's undo restoring 25274 exactly, wheel sizing clamped 2..400, a fresh mount seeded with the value restoring the identical drawing (the Reuse path), an unpainted step reporting null and deriving no file, 0 bare form controls. Numbers in validation.md.

THE raw/ RULE IS LIFTED (Fabio; commits 21987a71 + e7d11f1c). Agents may author comfy_workflows/raw/. key_decisions: THE raw/ BAN WAS AIMED AT THE WRONG TARGET, and lifting it cost nothing. The incident it cited (MPI-272, an API-format file in raw/) was a USER 'Export (API)' mis-click - the doc's own words are 'No script did it', and no agent did either. The real agent-side hazard, a bare workflow-to-api.mjs run that clobbered 7 runtime files on 2026-08-07, was already fixed in code by assertNotInRaw() (f918c907). What replaces the ban is a FORMAT law: raw/ is LiteGraph, never API JSON; comfy_workflows/*.json is BUILD OUTPUT, so hand-patching it is still wrong because the next convert reverts you.

THE AGENT HAD ALREADY MADE THE GRAPH - the card was never really waiting on Fabio. Session 5 BUILT it (build_graph.py) and POSTed it to /prompt, which is how the images were generated; it just left API format behind, because the old rule forbade writing raw/. Nothing was missing except the editable twin.

THE LITEGRAPH WAS OBTAINED FROM THE FRONTEND, NOT SYNTHESISED. There was no LiteGraph anywhere (bench-graph-blend.json AND the bench-store copy are both API). The ComfyUI frontend auto-lays-out an API import, so `await app.loadApiJson(api, name)` then `app.graph.serialize()` reads a real LiteGraph out of memory - no write to the bench, nothing queued. bench-editing.md forbids hand-writing LiteGraph nodes and it is right to: widget-to-input ordering is implicit and shifts silently.

THE BENCH-STORE COPY IS NOT THE REPO COPY, and every handoff has been quoting the wrong one. Bench = 74 nodes with 4 PreviewImage debug taps and Output_Image on a PreviewImage. Repo = 70 nodes with Output_Image on a SaveImage. The repo copy produced the measured results and is what ships. 'The 74-node graph' in this plan means the bench copy.

THE COMFYUI EDITOR QUANTISES FLOAT WIDGETS - a new trap, filed in bench-editing.md. ThresholdMask declares step 0.01, so the round trip rounded the signed-off thresholds 12/255 (0.047058...) and 40/255 (0.156862...) to 0.05 and 0.16. Converts clean, validates clean, runs - 6% off the value the region measurements were made against. Restored exactly in the raw file, located by matching round(target, 2) rather than a hardcoded widgets_values index. IT COMES BACK if anyone reopens that raw file in ComfyUI and saves.

The drawing IS persisted, as a PNG data URL in stepValues - the opposite of crop, whose derived file is stripped from the snapshot. Not arbitrary: a padded outpaint image is DERIVED and re-derivable from the rect, while a drawing is an INPUT made by hand with nothing to re-derive it from. 42 KB for a test scribble. Marked `ponytail:` with the preview-asset upgrade path named.

playwright-cli in this build CANNOT run a MULTI-LINE eval - it dies with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'` at 2:38 on a trivial two-line IIFE, which reads as a bug in your probe and is not one. Single line only. And the command line caps out around 8KB, so a large payload has to be chunked into `window.__x` across several evals (5 x 5000 chars worked) rather than passed as one argument.

Heredocs are blocked by a guard hook and HANG until the 2-minute timeout - twice this session. Write a .py or .js FILE and run it by path. Windows python also needs sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8') or it dies on a cp1252 charmap error mid-script.
